inspection_summary: Fresh isolated inspection of all 536 logical lines in the exact SHA-bound normalized source. Eight conservative semantic units were retained: reconstruct a variety by intrinsically recognizing point objects and then recovering line bundles, topology, and the structure sheaf; complete a fully faithful image by its orthogonal complement; represent an abstract exact fully faithful functor by a unique kernel on a product; test full faithfulness on point objects; decompose a blow-up category into the original category and shifted copies of the center; distinguish birational embeddings from equivalences and interpret directional simplification as removal of summands; contrast quotient, embedding, equivalence, and conjectural minimality in categorical desingularization; and replace a missing commutative geometric component by modules over a Koszul-dual sheaf algebra. This is a short survey: most theorems are stated with citations rather than proved in the source, and several generalizations, minimality claims, and birational-program interpretations are explicitly conjectural or expected. Novelty is unconfirmed because no #44 record, other corpus source, underlying cited paper, prior plan, alternate version, issue history, network resource, or corpus identity was consulted. The normalization is readable, but some diagrams, superscripts, orthogonal symbols, functor directions, and displayed decompositions require typeset verification.

accepted_units.title: Reconstruct geometry by intrinsically recognizing its point objects
accepted_units.why_material: The source uses the Serre functor as an internal categorical incarnation of the canonical bundle. Under an ampleness condition, point-supported objects can be recognized without external labels; from those objects one first recovers the underlying set, then line bundles, the Zariski topology, and finally the structure sheaf. The reusable move is staged reconstruction from intrinsic probes: identify atomic objects by a canonical endofunctor, then rebuild successively richer relations and structure rather than assuming the original presentation.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 2.2 is stated for smooth irreducible projective varieties with ample canonical or anticanonical sheaf and attributed to prior work; this survey gives only the proof idea. The orbifold extension is separately attributed. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: shift, dual, and tensor notation is mostly readable but exact categorical conventions should be checked in the typeset source/cited theorem. Representation limit: recognition occurs inside a graded derived category equipped with its Serre and translation functors, and reconstruction is only up to the stated equivalence/isomorphism. Scope limit: ampleness is essential in the theorem as stated; derived-equivalent varieties outside this regime need not be isomorphic, so the method cannot be generalized by dropping the hypothesis.

accepted_units.title: Complete a fully faithful image by its orthogonal complement
accepted_units.why_material: A fully faithful functor preserves all morphism data of its source but need not fill the target. The source identifies the unaccounted portion as an orthogonal subcategory and organizes the image plus complement into an ordered semiorthogonal decomposition that generates the target. This separates embedding from equivalence and turns a vague notion of extra information into a structurally testable component.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage gives definitions and examples via exceptional sequences, then proposes a motivic interpretation of semiorthogonal simplification. The definitions and decomposition mechanism are retained; the motive analogy is explicitly a proposal. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: orthogonal superscripts and angle-bracket decomposition notation are partially displaced by normalization. Representation limit: the complement is directional because semiorthogonality is ordered; left and right orthogonals need not coincide. Scope limit: a fully faithful image yields the claimed decomposition here in the admissible smooth-projective derived setting; an arbitrary full subcategory need not have adjoints or generate a semiorthogonal completion.

accepted_units.title: Encode an abstract fully faithful functor by a unique kernel on a product
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns an abstract functor into a geometric integral transform: pull an object to the product, tensor with a kernel, and push to the target. The representation theorem says every exact fully faithful functor in the stated setting arises this way, with the kernel unique up to isomorphism. The reusable move is to replace opaque action-on-all-objects data by a single relational object whose two projections implement transport.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 3.2 is stated and attributed to prior work; the survey notes why an earlier right-adjoint assumption can be removed. No proof is supplied here. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: derived pullback/tensor/pushforward symbols and projection order require typeset verification. Representation limit: kernels live in the derived category of the product and are unique only up to isomorphism while functors are compared up to natural isomorphism. Scope limit: the theorem assumes exact full faithfulness and smooth projective source and target; arbitrary triangulated functors or nonproper spaces need not have such a kernel representation.

accepted_units.title: Test full faithfulness on a spanning family of point objects
accepted_units.why_material: Instead of comparing every pair of objects, the source tests a kernel functor on skyscraper sheaves of closed points: distinct points must map to homologically orthogonal objects, while each image must have the prescribed self-Hom and Ext amplitude. This compresses a global functor property into pairwise tests on a canonical family and motivates constructing embeddings from moduli of orthogonal objects.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 3.3 gives the iff criterion under its stated hypotheses. The subsequent claim about moduli spaces with sheaves of noncommutative algebras is called an important principle and an expectation; the DG extension is only indicated. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: degree ranges and point subscripts are OCR-damaged in places, so the exact Ext conditions require typeset checking. Representation limit: the test uses closed-point skyscraper sheaves and a functor already represented by a kernel. Scope limit: the criterion assumes the stated smooth varieties and derived setting; the broader noncommutative moduli construction is not proved by the criterion and loss of orthogonality requires additional DG structure.

accepted_units.title: Decompose a blow-up into the original category and repeated center components
accepted_units.why_material: For a smooth blow-up, pullback preserves the original derived category fully faithfully, while functors through the exceptional divisor embed copies of the center's category with successive twists. Ordering these images produces a semiorthogonal decomposition of the blown-up category. The semantic move is to express a geometric surgery as preservation of the old component plus explicitly localized new information supported on the surgery center.
accepted_units.context_note: Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.2 are stated for a smooth variety blown up along a smooth center of codimension r and attributed to prior work. The survey does not reproduce their proofs. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the blow-up square, exceptional divisor notation, twists, and decomposition brackets are layout-damaged and require typeset verification. Representation limit: the components are functor images with an order and line-bundle twists, not a direct product of categories. Scope limit: smoothness of ambient variety and center and the standard blow-up geometry are essential; singular centers or other modifications need different formulas.

accepted_units.title: Read birational direction as embedding, and crepant symmetry as equivalence
accepted_units.why_material: In the proved elementary model, a flip gives a fully faithful functor in one direction, whereas the balanced flop case gives an equivalence. The source then interprets the general expected embedding as a semiorthogonal decomposition whose nontrivial orthogonal is removed when passing toward the birationally simpler model; for a flop the orthogonal vanishes. This provides a reusable distinction between loss-aware simplification and reversible change of representation.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 4.3 proves the special flip/flop statement under explicit projective normal-bundle hypotheses. Conjecture 4.4 generalizes it; the source notes a dimension-three proof and some special cases, while the minimal-model minimization language and moduli construction are suggestive. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the birational diagram, pull-push functor direction, divisor comparison, and some superscripts are damaged. Representation limit: direction is controlled by the canonical-divisor discrepancy and by a chosen correspondence/resolution. Scope limit: the general flip embedding and flop equivalence are conjectural as stated in the survey except for cited cases; a naive pull-push functor is explicitly said not always to be fully faithful.

accepted_units.title: Separate quotient recovery from minimal categorical resolution
accepted_units.why_material: A geometric resolution maps its derived category onto the singular category by quotienting out the invisible kernel. The source abstracts this as a categorical desingularization, then proposes a minimal one characterized by fully faithful embedding into every competitor. A sheaf of endomorphism algebras supplies a noncommutative candidate whose module category has finite homological dimension. The reusable move is to state explicitly what a resolution forgets under quotient and to compare resolutions by embeddings rather than by size metaphors.
accepted_units.context_note: The quotient observation is stated for proper birational maps to rational singularities. Existence/uniqueness of a minimal categorical desingularization is an expectation; Definition and Conjecture 5.1 give the noncommutative proposal, with the McKay relation as context. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: quotient-category, endomorphism-sheaf, and resolution symbols are partially malformed. Representation limit: the proposed resolution may be noncommutative and is represented by coherent modules over a sheaf algebra, not by points of a smooth space. Scope limit: rational/canonical singularity, finite homological dimension, finite cover, and crepancy hypotheses matter; minimality and universal embedding are conjectural, not consequences of the definition alone.

accepted_units.title: Replace a missing commutative component by a Koszul-dual sheaf algebra
accepted_units.why_material: For intersections of quadrics, a familiar commutative parameter curve accounts for a categorical component only in special low-dimensional cases. The source constructs the quadratic dual Clifford algebra, sheafifies an even subalgebra over the parameter space, and uses its module category as the persistent component. When ambient dimension exceeds twice the number of equations, exceptional objects form the complement; at equality, the noncommutative component is the entire category. The generic move is to preserve a dual description by widening from spaces to sheaves of algebras when commutative geometry no longer suffices.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 6.1 is stated without proof in the survey, followed by commutative, Azumaya, K3, moduli, and Koszul-duality interpretations. Exact status is a stated theorem under the listed hypotheses; generalization beyond them is only noted. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the graded-algebra, center, Veronese, sheafification, and decomposition formulas have displaced indices and require typeset verification. Representation limit: the component is D b of coherent right modules over a sheaf of finite noncommutative algebras and need not equal the derived category of an ordinary variety. Scope limit: the theorem assumes a smooth complete intersection of quadrics over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field with the stated dimension inequality; commutative recovery additionally depends on parity, the center cover, and Brauer/Azumaya conditions.

ecosystem_findings.summary: This source makes decomposition directional and semantic: an image is completed by an orthogonal, blow-up adds center-supported pieces, flips remove a nontrivial summand while flops do not, and a noncommutative component can coexist with exceptional objects. This strengthens a source-only saturation probe that asks what each component represents and whether decomposition signals reversible equivalence or information loss. Corpus novelty is unconfirmed.

Canonicality is operationalized through intrinsic point recognition, uniqueness of a functor kernel, a spanning-family criterion, and a conjectural minimal-resolution comparison by embeddings. The last is explicitly not established, so the source strengthens both positive tests and proof-status discipline for universal-property probes. Corpus novelty is unconfirmed.

The source ties reconstruction from the derived category to ampleness of the canonical or anticanonical bundle, which lets the Serre functor distinguish point objects. This is a source-grounded candidate geometry dependency; whether it is new or already represented elsewhere is unconfirmed.

The source suggests a provisional family in which equivalence, fully faithful embedding, and quotient encode different birational relationships: reversible change, directional simplification, and forgetting a kernel. General minimality claims remain conjectural, and corpus novelty of the family is explicitly unconfirmed.

remaining_meaningful_material: No additional unit was accepted after complete inspection. Meaningful but unretained material includes the autoequivalence-group classification, exceptional-sequence examples and braid actions, detailed flip diagrams and hypotheses, cited orbifold generalizations, special Azumaya/Brauer cases, and bibliographic provenance. These remain useful source context, but extracting them separately would narrow rather than extend the retained mechanisms, duplicate their roles, or depend on results only cited by this survey. Novelty of retained and unretained material is unconfirmed.
